## Answer: $\dfrac{138}{55}\approx 2.509$

**Setup.** The 12 cards have values 2, 3, 4, each appearing four times, so only the value sequence matters. A removal happens when the first pair of equal adjacent values appears in the remaining deck. Everything up to and including that pair is removed, and scanning restarts on the cards after it with no memory of the previous card.

**Markov structure.** Each unscanned suffix is a uniformly random arrangement of its remaining multiset. So the state is the multiset of remaining counts $(a,b,c)$ together with the value of the last drawn card in the current segment, which matters only for detecting a double.

Let $f(T)$ be the expected number of future removals from a fresh start with remaining counts $T$, and let $H^{(i)}(T)$ be the expected number when the last drawn card has value $i$ and $T$ is the remaining counts. Drawing the next card gives:

- $f(T)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_j T_j\,H^{(j)}(T-e_j)$
- $H^{(i)}(T)=f(T)+\frac{T_i}{n}\bigl(1+f(T-e_i)-H^{(i)}(T-e_i)\bigr)$

where $n=|T|$. The second identity follows from the first by eliminating the sum over $j\ne i$.

**Checks.** I verified several small cases directly by enumeration: $f(2,1,0)=2/3$, $f(2,1,1)=1/2$, $f(3,1,0)=1$, $f(2,2,0)=1$, and $H^{(2)}(2,2,0)=4/3$, $H^{(1)}(1,2,1)=3/4$, $H^{(3)}(3,1,1)=13/10$, among others. All matched the recursion.

**Computing the target.** Since $N$ counts removals, we need $f(4,4,4)$. Because $f(4,4,4)=\frac{1}{12}\cdot 3\cdot 4\cdot H^{(4)}(3,4,4)=H^{(4)}(3,4,4)$, it suffices to carry the recursion up through level 11. The key values are:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| $f(4,3,2)$ | $467/252$ |
| $H(1\mid 4,4)$ (level 9) | $139/63$ |
| $f(4,4,2)$ | $32/15$ |
| $H(2\mid 4,4)$ (level 10) | $104/45$ |
| $H(3\mid 4,3)$ (level 10) | $91/40$ |
| $f(3,4,4)$ | $377/165$ |

Then

$$f(4,4,4)=H(3\mid 4,4)=\frac{377}{165}+\frac{3}{11}\Bigl(1+\frac{32}{15}-\frac{104}{45}\Bigr)=\frac{377}{165}+\frac{37}{165}=\frac{414}{165}=\frac{138}{55}.$$

ANSWER: 138/55
